title: Guava Flow Cytometer Troubleshooting Protocol
author: Steven W Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iv9ce96

steps.title: Remove flow cell
steps.instruction: Take the flow cell out of the instrument; it will break if left in place.

steps.title: Power off instrument
steps.instruction: Turn off the flow cytometer using the toggle switch on the back of the machine.

steps.title: Unscrew top panel
steps.instruction: Remove the top panel by unscrewing the two Torx T‑10 screws in the tray bay at the top left and right, located under the door.

steps.title: Disconnect power and USB
steps.instruction: Unplug both the power‑supply cable and the USB connection from the back of the flow cytometer.

steps.title: Lift and slide hood
steps.instruction: Lift the front of the hood to greater than 45°, then slide the hood back away from the machine to free the back of the hood.

steps.title: Eject sampling tray
steps.instruction: Pull the sampling tray forward to the “eject” position; this may require some force.

steps.title: Reset sensor assembly
steps.instruction: Reset the motor/sensor assembly by first pushing the sensor (marked A) down to the bottom, then pushing it all the way up, taking care not to bend or break the thin metal piece on the bottom of the sensor.

substeps.instruction: Locate the extra motor in the drawer under the instrument (wrapped in bubble wrap) and pull it out to practice moving the assembly before handling the machine.
Manipulate the motor by pushing or pulling the black “L”‑shaped portion or the screw; do not push/pull the metal strip.

steps.title: Re‑position sampling tray
steps.instruction: Move the sampling tray as far back as it will go.

steps.title: Replace hood and panel
steps.instruction: Re‑assemble the hood and top panel in the reverse order of steps 4–7; you may replace the Torx screws after the machine initiates.

steps.title: Verify machine initiation
steps.instruction: If the instrument initiates (gears moving, etc.) continue; if not, ensure the sampling tray is fully back and the sensor is fully up.

steps.title: Enter capillary shutdown mode
steps.instruction: Set the system to capillary shutdown mode.
